overview: Infratil is a New Zealand-based infrastructure investment company (NZX: IFT, ASX: IFT) with a NZ$16 billion market capitalisation that owns and actively manages a portfolio of infrastructure assets across four key sectors: Digital Infrastructure (~57% of portfolio value), Renewable Energy (~22%), Healthcare (~13%), and Airports (~5%). Operating across 18+ countries in Australasia, North America, Asia and Europe, Infratil's portfolio is dominated by CDC Data Centres - now a globally scaled AI data centre platform with 1GW+ of contracted capacity - and Longroad Energy, a fast-growing US renewable developer. The company is externally managed by Morrison & Co and targets 11-15% annualised total shareholder returns over a rolling 10-year basis, having delivered 18.9% TSR since inception in 1994.

business_model.summary: Infratil generates returns through capital appreciation and distributions from its portfolio companies, funded by long-term contracted infrastructure revenues. The company is externally managed by Morrison & Co under a management agreement that includes performance-based incentive fees. CDC Data Centres (data centre leasing) and Longroad Energy (renewable power generation and development) are the primary growth engines; One NZ (telecommunications), Wellington Airport, and healthcare assets provide more stable cash generation.

revenue_streams.name: Other (Kao Data, Gurin, Galileo, Mint, Clearvision)

business_model.customer_type: Mix of B2B (data centres with hyperscaler/government tenants, wholesale energy, telecom infrastructure) and B2C (retail telecommunications, medical imaging, airport services)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia 47%, New Zealand 32%, United States 13%, Europe 5%, Asia 3%
business_model.portfolio_structure: Three-pillar approach: Pillar 1 (cash generators: One NZ, Wellington Airport, healthcare) providing stable distributions; Pillar 2 (scaling growth: CDC, Longroad Energy) driving asset value uplift; Pillar 3 (early-stage platforms: Gurin Energy, Galileo, Mint Renewables, Kao Data, Clearvision) seeding future growth

main_competitors: AustralianSuper and other super fund direct infrastructure investment
competitive_position.market_position: Leading infrastructure investment company in New Zealand; NZ$16 billion market cap; included in S&P/NZX 50, ASX 200 (since July 2025), and MSCI Global Standard Index. Rated BBB+ (stable) by S&P since December 2025. CDC is the leading data centre operator in Australasia and is becoming a globally relevant AI infrastructure platform.

moat_factors.factor: CDC's structural advantages in AI data centre supply
moat_factors.description: CDC holds 671MW operating, 572MW under construction, and a 2.9GW pipeline in Australasia. Long-duration contracts (30+ year with renewal options) with investment-grade counterparties (hyperscalers, government) provide earnings visibility. CDC's Baa2 (Moody's) credit rating and investment-grade institutional shareholder base support continued capital-efficient expansion.

moat_factors.factor: Long-term contracted revenue across the portfolio
moat_factors.description: Data centre contracts typically 10-30 years; renewable energy PPAs 15-25 years; regulated airport and telecom revenues. Provides strong downside protection and earnings predictability.

moat_factors.factor: Morrison & Co management expertise and origination
moat_factors.description: 30+ years of infrastructure investment experience across a global network. Established relationships with governments, hyperscalers, and institutional capital. Early mover advantage in CDC (2016 investment, 35.8% IRR) and Longroad (2016, 47.3% IRR) validates origination capability.

One NZ holds mobile spectrum licenses; Wellington Airport has a natural monopoly; CDC campuses benefit from power connections and planning approvals that are difficult to replicate; renewable projects hold development rights and grid connections.

Inaugural BBB+ (S&P, December 2025) enables access to broader debt markets and improved borrowing terms. Estimated annual savings of ~$7m in FY27, rising to ~$10m over time. Capital bonds programme (BBB-) further diversifies funding and provides 50% equity credit.

weaknesses: High concentration in CDC (43% of portfolio value) creates single-asset sensitivity to AI demand cycles and execution risk
New Zealand economic exposure across One NZ, Wellington Airport, healthcare assets and RHCNZ (~32% of geographic exposure)
External management structure incurs both base management fees and performance-based incentive fees that reduce net returns
Corporate net debt increased to NZ$3.2 billion (LTV 15.4%), materially higher than NZ$2.2 billion in FY25, increasing interest burden
Smaller scale than global mega-funds; share price at a discount to consensus analyst targets

growth_drivers: CDC AI data centre supercycle: contracted capacity now exceeds 1GW following the landmark 555MW deal (announced 5 May 2026, largest data centre contract in Australian history). CDC targets A$680-720m EBITDAF in FY27 (+73-83% on FY26), exceeding A$1bn in FY28, with fully deployed 1GW contracted capacity expected to generate ~A$2bn annualised EBITDAF. CDC has also mandated an inaugural AMTN hybrid bond to fund growth without requiring further shareholder equity injection.

Longroad Energy US renewable acceleration: Longroad closed FY26 with 3.5GW operational, 2GW under construction, and agreed to acquire a ~2.8GW solar and storage project (subject to regulatory approvals). Infratil committed a further US$300m over two years to support this step-up. Longroad targets ~US$490m Opco run-rate EBITDAF in CY26 and US$1bn by CY29/30 as annual development cadence rises to ~2GW.

Longroad data centre co-location strategy: Longroad is actively developing options for 4GW+ of grid-connected data centres co-located with its solar and storage assets, creating a new revenue stream at the intersection of its renewable and digital infrastructure capabilities.

Portfolio divestment and capital recycling: NZ$600m of asset sales completed (Manawa to Contact, RetireAustralia NZ$331m, Infratil Property NZ$55m, Fortysouth >NZ$200m). Qscan sale process underway. Post-balance date, NZ$495m raised from selling 5% of Contact Energy. Management flags potential for another NZ$1bn+ of divestments in the medium term, with proceeds redeployed into higher-return growth platforms.

Kao Data UK expansion: Revenue grew 28% to £48m in FY26. New 30MW+ West London greenfield site (4.7-acre Tier 1 availability zone) acquired, targeted for 2029 delivery. KLON-03 (17.6MW, GPU-optimised, up to 130kW rack density) under construction with capacity online from early 2027. Materially all current capacity contracted.

Broadening shareholder base: ASX 200 inclusion (July 2025) has lifted ASX trading volume to ~30% of total. Growing Australian institutional ownership. Expanded analyst coverage. These factors support valuation discovery and reduce NAV discount.

ESG ratings uplift: MSCI ESG upgraded from A to AA; GRESB score 94 (vs 86 prior year); inclusion in Dow Jones Best in Class Australia Index. Improving sustainability credentials attract ESG-mandated capital.

business.description: CDC represents approximately 43% of total portfolio asset value at NZ$8.9bn. A disappointment in AI data centre demand - whether from hyperscaler capex pullbacks, alternative compute architectures, oversupply, or execution delays on the 555MW contract - could have an outsized negative impact on Infratil's NAV and share price.

While current contract momentum is exceptional, the AI infrastructure build-out is unprecedented in scale and speed. Demand depends on continued hyperscaler capex, regulatory treatment of AI, and the economics of AI-driven workloads. Disruption from efficiency breakthroughs (e.g., next-generation model architectures) or a broader AI investment pause could slow future contract signings beyond 1GW.

Persistent macroeconomic headwinds in NZ affect One NZ (EBITDAF grew only modestly at NZ$609m, flat in real terms), Wellington Airport domestic passengers (down 6% to 4.26m), and healthcare imaging volumes. NZ accounts for 32% of geographic exposure.

Galileo recognised write-offs and write-downs of €61.2m (IFT share €23.3m) in FY26 as early-stage development values fell across European markets moving to maturity. Strategy has been reset toward fewer markets and independent power producer model, but execution of the reset carries risk. IRR has been modest (9.9% over 6 years).

business.risk: Gurin Energy - Project Vanda approval uncertainty
business.description: Project Vanda (2GW Indonesian solar, subsea export to Singapore; US$2-3bn capex) obtained Indonesia's production licence in March 2026 but is still awaiting the export licence as the key gate to final investment decision. Prolonged delays risk stranding development capital and opportunity cost.

financial.description: Infratil's corporate net debt increased from NZ$2.2bn to NZ$3.2bn in FY26, driven by the A$500m CDC equity injection (February 2026) and Contact Energy acquisition costs. LTV ratio rose to 15.4% (from 12.8%). Although the BBB+ credit rating provides access to capital markets, elevated debt increases interest costs and reduces headroom for unexpected events. Weighted average cost of drawn debt was 5.20% with a short average tenor of 2.7 years.

Approximately 65% of portfolio value is in offshore assets denominated in AUD, USD, GBP and EUR. CDC and Qscan (AUD), Longroad (USD), Kao Data (GBP), and Galileo/Gurin (USD/EUR). NZD strength would reduce the NZD value of offshore earnings and asset valuations. FX forecast assumptions: AUD 0.8382, USD 0.5769, EUR 0.4958, GBP 0.4368.

Infratil lodged a PDS for inaugural capital bonds (BBB-, 50% equity credit) on 26 May 2026. Successful issuance is important to maintain the investment grade credit profile and diversify funding sources. Market conditions, investor demand, and pricing remain uncertain.

Infratil has committed US$300m (approximately NZ$520m at guidance rates) to Longroad over the next ~2 years on top of existing commitments. This is a large call on capital that will need to be funded through asset divestments, operating distributions, and/or debt.

regulatory.description: Longroad's project economics rely on the Inflation Reduction Act tax credit framework. Solar projects must be placed in service by end of 2030 for full credit eligibility. Any legislative changes reducing or eliminating IRA credits (e.g., through budget reconciliation) could impair project economics. Longroad has >6GW of tax-qualified pipeline supporting development targets to 2030.

One NZ is subject to Commerce Commission oversight on pricing, spectrum, and infrastructure sharing. Mobile termination rates, fibre access pricing, and future spectrum allocations all affect One NZ's economics.

Wellington Airport aeronautical pricing is reviewed by the Commerce Commission. Input methodologies and price path determinations constrain revenue growth. Current BBB (S&P, stable) rating supports access to capital at competitive rates.

Increasing data localisation requirements and potential AI-specific regulation could affect CDC's customer mix, facility requirements, or operational model. Australia's National AI Plan currently identifies CDC-style infrastructure as foundational, but regulatory evolution could change incentive structures.

macro.risk: Interest rate and discount rate sensitivity
macro.description: Infrastructure assets are valued using discounted cash flow models. Sustained elevated interest rates compress asset multiples and increase funding costs across all portfolio companies. Infratil's own weighted average cost of debt was 5.20% with a short 2.7-year average tenor, creating refinancing risk if rates remain elevated.

CDC's growth ambitions depend on procuring sufficient grid-connected power in Australia. Delays in grid upgrades, constraints on power procurement, or higher-than-expected electricity costs could slow CDC's build programme or compress margins. CDC's WUE of less than 0.02 and 100% renewable electricity offering mitigate some constraint risk.

US tariff policies affect the cost of solar panels, batteries, and data centre equipment imported for Longroad and CDC/Longroad projects. Higher equipment costs could impair project economics, particularly for large-scale solar developments with construction starting from CY28.

Wellington Airport and NZ assets are exposed to seismic and weather risks. The completed runway safety upgrade (March 2026) now enables long-haul flights to Asia. Hydro generation and renewables are exposed to changing precipitation patterns. Infratil scored B on CDP climate disclosure (up from C prior year).

execution.description: Delivering 555MW of contracted capacity across campuses with construction and customer activation scheduled through FY28-29 is an unprecedented build programme for CDC. Current 572MW under construction and FY27 capex guidance of A$3.8-4.2bn represent a step-change in capital deployment. Delays in construction, power procurement, or customer activation would defer the associated EBITDAF ramp.

The Qscan sale process (NZ$590m at independent valuation) is underway but in a challenging M&A environment. Closing transactions at book value is not guaranteed. Meanwhile, NZ$495m Contact Energy proceeds (post-balance date block trade at NZ$9.25/share) reduces Infratil's Contact stake to ~9% and this capital must be productively redeployed.

RHCNZ Medical Imaging EBITDAF was flat at NZ$63.6m while valuation declined NZ$73m to NZ$616m, reflecting challenging trading conditions, cost pressures and revised long-term growth assumptions. A performance improvement programme is underway but the IRR since inception of 8.6% is below Infratil's targets.

In FY26, incentive fee calculations produced a net negative position (NZ$39.4m), as outperformance at CDC was more than offset by underperformance at Galileo, Gurin, Longroad and others. The negative fee carries forward to reduce future payables. The structure reduces near-term fee leakage but creates uncertainty around future obligations when CDC outperforms.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global infrastructure investment is benefiting from structural megatrends: AI and cloud computing driving unprecedented data centre demand; decarbonisation driving renewable energy investment; government infrastructure deficits creating private capital opportunities. The AI data centre build-out is creating a multi-year demand supercycle for digital infrastructure assets. Global infrastructure investment returns are expected at 8-12% over the cycle, with premium digital infrastructure assets commanding higher multiples.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate. The portfolio is structured to provide downside protection through long-term contracts (data centres, PPAs) and regulated/monopoly assets (airport, telecom), while CDC and Longroad provide significant upside to the AI/energy transition thematic. Economic sensitivity is meaningful through One NZ consumer revenues, Wellington Airport domestic traffic, and healthcare volumes (~35-40% of earnings).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - both directly (Infratil's NZ$3.2bn corporate net debt at 5.20% weighted average cost) and indirectly (discount rates compress infrastructure asset valuations when rates are elevated). The BBB+ rating and capital bonds initiative reduce refinancing risk but do not eliminate it.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Significant - approximately 65% of portfolio is in offshore assets (AUD 47%, USD 13%, GBP/EUR 5%). NZD appreciation reduces NZD values of offshore earnings and asset valuations. Guidance prepared using AUD 0.8382, USD 0.5769, EUR 0.4958, GBP 0.4368.
key_input_costs: Electricity (data centre operations - CDC passes through or hedges power costs)
Construction materials and equipment (solar panels, batteries, data centre build-out)
Interest rates (debt funding across Infratil parent and all portfolio companies)
Technology equipment (servers, GPUs, telecom network gear - tariff sensitive)

recent_developments.event: Infratil lodged a PDS for inaugural capital bonds (BBB-, 50% equity credit under S&P framework), with presentation released 2 June 2026. Adds long-duration funding diversity alongside the BBB+ rated parent entity. Bank debt refinancing in May 2026 also realised cost savings and improved terms.

Post-balance date: sold 5% stake in Contact Energy (53.5m shares at NZ$9.25) via fully underwritten block trade, raising ~NZ$495m. Reduces Contact holding to ~9%. Proceeds enhance liquidity and fund CDC and Longroad growth; Infratil committed to retaining remaining Contact stake until at least FY26 results in August 2026.

FY2026 annual results announced 26 May 2026: Proportionate Operational EBITDAF NZ$989m (+11%), total asset value NZ$20.6bn (+13%), NAV NZ$16.26/share (+5%). Net parent surplus NZ$549.8m (up NZ$845m from FY25 loss, driven by strong revaluations and discontinued operations). FY27 EBITDAF guidance NZ$1,300-$1,400m, implying ~21% increase. Final dividend 13.65 cents per share (ex-date 9 June, pay date 29 June 2026).

CDC announced 555MW data centre contract (5 May 2026) with an unnamed US investment-grade customer on a 30-year term (plus 20-year renewal options). Australia's largest-ever data centre contract, lifting CDC's total contracted capacity beyond 1GW. CDC FY27 EBITDAF guidance A$680-720m; expected to exceed A$1bn in FY28 and reach ~A$2bn annualised when fully deployed. CDC was assigned a Baa2 (stable) credit rating by Moody's on 21 April 2026.

Longroad Energy agreed to acquire a ~2.8GW solar and battery storage development project in the US (PPA in place; construction in two phases in CY28/CY29, subject to state regulatory approvals and land lease extension). Infratil committed additional US$300m equity to support Longroad's accelerated development cadence targeting ~2GW per annum. Longroad targets US$1bn run-rate EBITDAF by CY29/30.

Fortysouth divestment completed post balance date (announced November 2025). Proceeds to Infratil exceeded NZ$200m (20% stake). Infratil received unconditional proceeds of NZ$217m, which were included in the LTV calculation at 31 March 2026.

S&P assigned Infratil an inaugural BBB+ (stable) credit rating in December 2025. RetireAustralia (50% stake, NZ$331m) and Infratil Property (NZ$55m) sales both completed December 2025. Anytime Radiology established as standalone teleradiology provider carved out from Qscan and RHCNZ.

Infratil acquired additional 4.92% stake in Contact Energy for NZ$438m (50% cash, 50% new Infratil shares), increasing ownership to 14.3%. Subsequently reduced Contact stake to ~9% via May 2026 block trade.

Infratil Investor Day outlined three-pillar portfolio strategy and medium-term KPIs. Strategic review of Qscan (59.5% stake, valued at NZ$590m at FY26) announced as part of portfolio simplification. Sale process is underway with an update expected in H1 FY27.

Added to S&P/ASX 200 Index, lifting Australian institutional ownership and ASX trading volume to ~30% of total. Contact Energy received Manawa Energy assets and Infratil received Contact Energy shares plus NZ$186m cash, increasing Infratil's Contact stake.

Reflects contracted capacity coming online. CDC EBITDAF expected to exceed A$1bn in FY28. Fully deployed 1GW contracted capacity expected to deliver ~A$2bn annualised EBITDAF. Guidance subject to build delivery timing and customer activation.

Modest uplift as construction completes in back-end of FY27 and FY28. Opco run-rate EBITDAF on track for ~US$490m across 7.1GW operating and under-construction fleet by end FY27. Development expenses increase as cadence ramps to 2GW p.a. Longroad targets US$1bn run-rate EBITDAF by CY29/30.

Runway safety upgrade enables long-haul flights to Asia. Despite easing capacity constraints, fuel costs limiting airline expansion. Domestic schedule reductions by airlines amid Middle East uncertainty.
Performance improvement programme focused on pricing, productivity and cost-saving. Public and private healthcare imaging demand growing.
Strategic sale process underway; update expected H1 FY27. Business performing strongly. 1.5m scans, 192 radiologists, 80 standalone clinics.
Increase reflects ramp in Gurin Energy, Galileo (post strategy reset) and Mint Renewables development activity.

items.notes: From FY27, corporate costs are disclosed separately from the Proportionate Operational EBITDAF guidance. Includes management fees, interest and overhead. Excludes incentive fees.
CDC accounts for A$3,800-4,200m (100% basis) as the 555MW contract programme accelerates. Longroad US$1,500-1,700m (100% basis). Kao Data £175-195m. One NZ NZ$235-265m.
Supports Longroad's development cadence uplift to ~2GW p.a. and the 2.8GW solar and storage acquisition (subject to regulatory approvals).

items.vs_prior: raised (initial NZ$1bn target now substantially met; Qscan and potential further divestments to come)
items.notes: NZ$600m of sales completed to FY26 end. Qscan sale process underway. NZ$495m Contact Energy block trade post-balance date. Management indicated potential for another NZ$1bn+ of medium-term divestments.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jason Boyes described CDC as having a 'once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to develop AI infrastructure at globally relevant scale.' Management expressed confidence that the AI data centre demand environment remains robust and that CDC's contracted growth pipeline underpins a significant step change in earnings over FY27-FY29. Longroad's increased US$300m equity commitment reflects accelerating opportunity in the US renewable and data centre co-location market. Portfolio simplification is ongoing, with Qscan sale expected to provide additional capital reallocation flexibility. The BBB+ rating and capital bonds initiative improve financial flexibility. Management acknowledged Galileo's strategy reset and Gurin's pending export licence approval as key near-term uncertainties.

bull_case: CDC earnings supercycle just beginning: With 1GW+ contracted (vs 220MW invoiced at FY26 end) and 572MW under construction, CDC EBITDAF is set to compound from A$393m in FY26 to A$680-720m in FY27 and exceed A$1bn in FY28. Fully deployed 1GW contracted capacity equates to ~A$2bn annualised EBITDAF. If CDC sustains its historical 35.8% IRR trajectory as AI infrastructure demand grows, CDC alone could be worth multiples of today's implied portfolio value.

Dual convergence platform in data and renewables: Infratil is uniquely positioned as a large-scale owner of both digital infrastructure (CDC, Kao Data) and renewable energy (Longroad, Gurin, Galileo, Mint). Longroad's 4GW+ data centre co-location options and its power supply relationships with hyperscalers create competitive moats and cross-platform synergies unavailable to pure-play peers.

Portfolio rerating with NAV discount potential narrowing: Consensus analyst price target of NZ$17.21 (9 analysts) is approximately 8-9% above the current share price of ~NZ$15.87, while NAV is NZ$16.26. ASX 200 inclusion (FY25), BBB+ credit rating (December 2025), and growing offshore investor base continue to broaden Infratil's shareholder pool. Successful Qscan divestment and capital bonds execution could further catalyse a rating uplift.

Strong track record of value creation with proven management: 18.9% annualised TSR since 1994 inception, 21.0% over 10 years. Morrison & Co's 30+ year infrastructure track record and early mover positions in CDC (35.8% IRR) and Longroad (47.3% IRR) demonstrate exceptional origination discipline. FY27 EBITDAF guidance of NZ$1.3-1.4bn (vs NZ$989m in FY26) implies the portfolio is entering a new earnings phase.

Balance sheet now investment grade with multiple capital avenues: BBB+ (S&P) parent rating, CDC Baa2 (Moody's), Wellington Airport BBB (S&P). Inaugural capital bonds (BBB-, 50% equity credit) diversify long-duration funding. Contact Energy block trade (NZ$495m) plus Qscan sale proceeds will provide additional capital flexibility. Weighted average debt cost of 5.20% expected to fall as BBB+ benefit flows through, saving ~$7-10m per annum.
bear_case: CDC concentration risk in an AI infrastructure cycle: CDC is 43% of portfolio value and effectively drives the entire thesis. If hyperscaler capex moderates, technology efficiency gains reduce compute demand, or the 555MW contract delivery encounters significant delays, the impact on Infratil's NAV could be severe with limited portfolio diversification to offset. The AI data centre build-out is a novel and unproven demand cycle at this scale.

Exploding capital requirements reduce free cash flow for years: Proportionate capital expenditure guidance of NZ$3.8-4.4bn in FY27 alone (vs NZ$2.7bn in FY26, +53%) reflects a portfolio in heavy build mode. Despite EBITDAF growth, free cash flow generation remains constrained while CDC's contracted pipeline is delivered and Longroad's 2GW p.a. cadence is established. Sustained equity dilution (Infratil issued shares for Contact Energy acquisition) and growing corporate net debt (NZ$3.2bn, LTV 15.4%) increase financial risk.

Corporate net debt and short tenor create refinancing vulnerability: Net debt grew from NZ$2.2bn to NZ$3.2bn (+46%) in FY26. Weighted average tenor is only 2.7 years. If rates remain elevated at refinancing or markets tighten, Infratil faces higher funding costs that compress both net returns to shareholders and asset valuations. The capital bonds programme is untested in terms of investor demand.

Longroad US policy risk and construction cadence challenges: Longroad's 2GW p.a. development ambition depends on IRA tax credits surviving the current US political environment, the 2.8GW acquisition receiving state regulatory and federal land approvals, and sustained hyperscaler demand for renewable power PPAs. Construction at record ~2GW simultaneously in multiple US states increases operational complexity and potential cost overruns.

Multiple sub-portfolio challenges persisting: RHCNZ valuation fell NZ$73m to NZ$616m (IRR 8.6%) on deteriorating trading. Galileo wrote off €61.2m of European development projects (IRR 9.9%). Gurin's Vanda project is still awaiting Indonesia's export licence. One NZ EBITDAF growth was minimal (NZ$609m, essentially flat) against a persistently weak NZ economy. These drags consume management bandwidth and capital that could otherwise be deployed in higher-return opportunities.
